body.statement: Uniformly over the instrumental fixed-radius subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the construction in \(\texttt{def:cross-fitted-primitive}\) satisfies \(\max_k\|\widehat h_k-h\|_{\infty}=O_P(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n})\) for \(h\in\{p,g,m,r\}\), where \(\beta=1/2-(d+1)/(4s)>5/12\), and \(\|\widehat\theta'-\theta'\|_{\infty,J}=O_P(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n})\), where \(\beta_1=1/2-(d+3)/(4s)>0\). These are consequences to be proved from the strengthened fixed-radius conditions, not assumptions imported from a comparator.
body.justification: This derives concrete nuisance rates on the explicitly instrumental smooth subclass before checking them against the separate Gumbel-scale remainder threshold.
body.gap: Doss (2026) formulates pointwise product-remainder conditions and Takatsu and Westling (2025) analyze different local-linear uniform remainders; neither source assumes or supplies this proposal's common global fixed-radius \(C^s\) class.
body.consumer: The displayed exponents can guide a future fully specified implementation, but are not yet a theorem about the frozen learner map.

obligation.what_is_open: A theorem for the frozen learner construction requires one fully specified sample map, including the kernel, boundary moment system, normalization map, and singular empirical Gram-matrix convention.
obligation.obstruction: Those implementation choices are absent from the frozen symbol and definition, so uniform inverse and derivative bounds cannot be asserted for the named estimator itself.
obligation.attempted: The boundary dimension, bias, stochastic term, derivative cost, both exponents, and stability of quotient and integration operations were derived for a regular complete implementation.
obligation.partial_result:
Put \(D=d+1\).  For a fully specified boundary local-polynomial sample map with a compactly supported bounded kernel, polynomial degree at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), uniformly invertible boundary moment matrices, and a declared output on singular empirical Gram matrices, Taylor expansion and a uniform Bernstein bound give, for derivative order \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\|\partial_a^j\widehat h_k-\partial_a^jh\|_\infty
=O_P\!\left(h_n^{s-j}+\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{D+2j}}}\right).
\]
At \(h_n=n^{-1/(2s)}\), the stochastic term dominates the bias, so
\[
\|\widehat h_k-h\|_\infty
=O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
\qquad \beta=\frac12-\frac{d+1}{4s},
\]
and
\[
\|\partial_a\widehat m_k-\partial_am\|_\infty
=O_P\!\left(n^{-\beta_1}\sqrt{\log n}\right),
\qquad \beta_1=\frac12-\frac{d+3}{4s}.
\]
The model inequality \(s>3(d+1)\) yields
\[
\beta>\frac12-\frac1{12}=\frac5{12},
\qquad
\beta_1>\frac12-\frac{d+3}{12(d+1)}>0.
\]
Stable division by a density bounded away from zero and integration over the unit covariate cube preserve these orders.  Thus these are the advertised rates for any completely specified regular implementation, but the frozen learner description does not define the kernel, boundary moment equations, normalization map, or singular-matrix output and hence does not yet define the sample map to which this argument can be applied.
